answer: The mirror records attestation edges. An operator's kth identity must sit outside a horizon of k edges separating it from every prior identity under that operator, and each edge on that horizon holds one velvet locked for the identity. The first identity needs a horizon of one edge and one velvet; the tenth ten; the thousandth a thousand. Because no edge may serve two horizons under one operator, a thousand identities lock 500,500 velvet. A fresh key is signed into the old mirror and inherits its horizon, so splitting cannot reset the count.
